59		// hops is what the engine reported so far; the table shows
60		// visiblePathHops(hops). At done it is replaced by Result.Hops.
61		hops   []nettrace.Hop
62		result *nettrace.Result
63		// errText is the persistent footer error of a run that never traced. It is
64		// cleared by a change of the field or by the next launch, not by a timer.
65		errText string
66	
67		// gen identifies the run whose messages are accepted; cancel and msgs
68		// belong to that run.
69		gen    int
70		cancel context.CancelFunc
71		msgs   <-chan tea.Msg
72	
73		footer components.FooterMessage
74	}
75	
76	func newPathModel(e pathEngine) *PathModel {
77		in := textinput.New()
78		theme.StyleTextInput(&in)
79		in.Placeholder = "hostname or IPv4 address[:port]"
80		in.CharLimit = pathInputCharLimit
81		in.Focus()
82	
83		return &PathModel{
84			engine:         e,
85			resolveTimeout: defaultPathResolveTimeout,
86			input:          in,
87			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[pathStep]{
88				Columns:    pathColumns(),
89				SortColumn: -1, // the path order is the content
90			}),
91		}
92	}
93	
94	// InEditMode reports whether the target field has the keyboard.
95	func (pm *PathModel) InEditMode() bool { return pm.state == pathEditing }
96	
97	func (pm *PathModel) running() bool { return pm.state == pathRunning }
98	
99	func (pm *PathModel) resize(width, height int) {
100		pm.width = width
101		pm.input.SetWidth(max(width-ansi.StringWidth(pathBarLabel)-4, 10))
102		pm.table.Resize(width, max(height, 3))
103	}
104	
105	// launchable is the one answer to "can a trace start here", read by the header
106	// and by the handler (Rule 130).
107	func (pm *PathModel) launchable() shortcut.Availability {
108		if pm.engine.supported() != nil {
109			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonPathUnsupported)
110		}
111		return shortcut.Availability{}
112	}
113	
114	func (pm *PathModel) update(msg tea.Msg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
115		switch msg := msg.(type) {
116		case pathResolvedMsg:
117			return pm.handleResolved(msg)
118		case pathHopMsg:
119			return pm.handleHop(msg)
120		case pathDoneMsg:
121			return pm.handleDone(msg)
122		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
123			return pm.handleKey(msg)
124		case tea.PasteMsg:
125			return pm.handlePaste(msg)
126		}
127		// Anything else is a footer expiry or the cursor blink of the field: the
128		// field needs the blink itself, or its cursor freezes.
129		pm.footer.Handle(msg)
130		var cmd tea.Cmd
131		pm.input, cmd = pm.input.Update(msg)
132		return pm, cmd
133	}
134	
135	func (pm *PathModel) handleResolved(msg pathResolvedMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
136		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
137			return pm, nil
138		}
139		pm.addr = msg.addr
140		route := newPathRoute(msg.route, msg.routeErr)
141		pm.route = &route
142		pm.refreshSteps()
143		return pm, waitForPathMsg(pm.msgs)
144	}
145	
146	func (pm *PathModel) handleHop(msg pathHopMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
147		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
148			return pm, nil
149		}
150		pm.hops = append(pm.hops, msg.hop)
151		pm.refreshSteps()
152		return pm, waitForPathMsg(pm.msgs)
153	}
154	
155	func (pm *PathModel) handleDone(msg pathDoneMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
156		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
157			return pm, nil
158		}
159		pm.releaseRun()
160		if msg.err != nil {
161			pm.hops = nil
162			pm.route = nil
163			pm.table.SetItems(nil)
164			pm.errText = pathErrorLabel(pm.target.Host, msg.err)
165			pm.state = pathEditing
166			return pm, pm.input.Focus()
167		}
168		res := msg.result
169		pm.result = &res
170		pm.hops = res.Hops
171		pm.refreshSteps()
172		pm.state = pathDone
173		return pm, nil
174	}
175	
176	// refreshSteps rebuilds the table rows from the route and the hops.
177	func (pm *PathModel) refreshSteps() { pm.table.SetItems(pathSteps(pm.route, pm.hops)) }
178	
179	// hopCount is the number of hop rows (the local rows are not counted).
180	func (pm *PathModel) hopCount() int {
181		n := 0
182		for _, s := range pm.table.Items() {
183			if s.Kind == stepHop {
184				n++
185			}
186		}
187		return n
188	}
189	
190	// releaseRun cancels the run's context (releasing it) and forgets its channel.
191	func (pm *PathModel) releaseRun() {
192		if pm.cancel != nil {
193			pm.cancel()
194			pm.cancel = nil
195		}
196		pm.msgs = nil
197	}
198	
199	func isPathNavKey(key string) bool {
200		switch key {
201		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end":
202			return true
203		}
204		return false
205	}
206	
207	func (pm *PathModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
208		key := msg.String()
209		if isPathNavKey(key) {
210			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
211		}
212		switch pm.state {
213		case pathEditing:
214			return pm.handleEditKey(msg)
215		case pathRunning:
216			if key == "esc" {
217				return pm.cancelRun()
218			}
219		case pathDone:
220			switch key {
221			case "enter":
222				return pm.launch(pm.target)
223			case "esc":
224				pm.state = pathEditing
225				return pm, pm.input.Focus()
226			}
227		}
228		return pm, nil
229	}
230	
231	func (pm *PathModel) handleEditKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
232		switch msg.String() {
233		case "enter":
234			return pm.launchFromInput()
235		case "esc", "tab", "shift+tab":
236			return pm, nil
237		}
238		return pm.updateInput(msg)
239	}
240	
241	func (pm *PathModel) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
242		if pm.state != pathEditing {
243			return pm, nil // a paste reaches the focused field only (Rule 111)
244		}
245		return pm.updateInput(msg)
246	}
247	
248	// updateInput hands msg to the field; a changed value drops the stale error.
249	func (pm *PathModel) updateInput(msg tea.Msg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
250		before := pm.input.Value()
251		var cmd tea.Cmd
252		pm.input, cmd = pm.input.Update(msg)
253		if pm.input.Value() != before {
254			pm.errText = ""
255		}
256		return pm, cmd
257	}
258	
259	func (pm *PathModel) launchFromInput() (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
260		tg, err := parsePathTarget(pm.input.Value())
261		if err != nil {
262			return pm, pm.footer.Error(capitalize(err.Error()))
263		}
264		return pm.launch(tg)
265	}
266	
267	// launch starts a run: the model changes here, in Update; the Cmd only does I/O.
268	func (pm *PathModel) launch(tg pathTarget) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
269		if a := pm.launchable(); !a.Enabled() {
270			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
271		}
272		pm.releaseRun()
273		pm.gen++
274		pm.target = tg
275		pm.addr = netip.Addr{}
276		pm.hops = nil
277		pm.route = nil
278		pm.result = nil
279		pm.errText = ""
280		pm.footer.Clear()
281		pm.table.SetItems(nil)
282	
283		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
284		ch := make(chan tea.Msg, pathChanCap)
285		pm.cancel, pm.msgs = cancel, ch
286		pm.input.Blur()
287		pm.state = pathRunning
288		return pm, startPathRun(ctx, pm.gen, tg, pm.resolveTimeout, pm.engine, ch)
289	}
290	
291	// cancelRun answers esc at once: the run's late messages are dropped by the
292	// generation bump, the hops already seen stay on screen.
293	func (pm *PathModel) cancelRun() (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
294		pm.releaseRun()
295		pm.gen++
296		pm.result = &nettrace.Result{Outcome: nettrace.OutcomeCancelled}
297		pm.state = pathDone
298		return pm, nil
299	}
300	
301	// startPathRun builds the launch Cmd from values only, so that no closure
302	// reads the model (Rule 110).
303	func startPathRun(ctx context.Context, gen int, tg pathTarget, timeout time.Duration, e pathEngine, ch chan tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
304		return tea.Batch(
305			func() tea.Msg {
306				producePath(ctx, gen, tg, timeout, e, ch)
307				return nil
308			},
309			waitForPathMsg(ch),
310		)
311	}

1	package docker
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os/exec"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/engine"
10	)
11	
12	// dockerCmd describes one CLI invocation.
13	type dockerCmd struct {
14		// Args are passed to the binary verbatim, e.g. {"ps", "--format", "..."}.
15		Args []string
16		// Stdin is written to the process when non-empty. Used to keep secrets out
17		// of the process list (`<engine> login --password-stdin`).
18		Stdin string
19		// Combined merges stderr into the returned bytes. Both engines write failure
20		// detail to stderr, so mutating calls set this to produce a usable message;
21		// calls that parse stdout leave it false.
22		Combined bool
23		// Helper runs `<engine>-credential-<Helper>` instead of the engine itself.
24		Helper string
25		// Ctx kills the process when it is cancelled. Nil for the invocations
26		// nobody can stop — which is all of them but the pull, the one long call
27		// this package makes that `K` is offered on (jobs.KindPull.Cancellable).
28		// A nil Ctx builds exactly the command it built before.
29		Ctx context.Context
30	}
31	
32	// dockerRunner is the seam every CLI invocation in this package passes through.
33	//
34	// The package talks to the engine's CLI rather than to an SDK, which keeps the
35	// dependency light but makes the whole package untestable without a daemon.
36	// Routing through this interface lets tests exercise the argument building and
37	// output parsing — the parts that actually carry defects — against canned
38	// output.
39	//
40	// It is also what made podman cheap (§3.67): the binary name was written in
41	// exactly one implementation of this interface, so the engine became a value
42	// without any call site moving.
43	type dockerRunner interface {
44		// LookPath reports whether the engine's binary is reachable on PATH.
45		LookPath() error
46		// Run executes one invocation and returns its captured output.
47		Run(cmd dockerCmd) ([]byte, error)
48		// Build returns a ready-to-run command without executing it, for callers
49		// that hand the process to a terminal (tea.ExecProcess).
50		Build(args ...string) *exec.Cmd
51	}
52	
53	// cliRunner is the production dockerRunner: it shells out to the real binary.
54	//
55	// It holds no engine of its own and reads engine.Current() on every call. A
56	// field would be a second place the resolved engine lives, and the two would
57	// be free to disagree after a context switch — which is exactly the kind of
58	// drift the one-runner seam exists to prevent.
59	type cliRunner struct{}
60	
61	func (cliRunner) LookPath() error {
62		_, err := exec.LookPath(engine.Current().Binary)
63		return err
64	}
65	
66	func (cliRunner) Build(args ...string) *exec.Cmd {
67		return exec.Command(engine.Current().Binary, args...) //nolint:gosec // the binary is a declared engine name or a path the user configured
68	}
69	
70	// credentialHelperPrefix names a credential helper binary, under both engines.
71	//
72	// Podman does not have a prefix of its own: measured on 2026-09-25, podman
73	// 5.7.0 with `credHelpers: {"host": "fake"}` ran docker-credential-fake for
74	// both `get` and `store` while a podman-credential-fake sat next to it on
75	// PATH, never called. A podman-specific prefix (§3.67) sent every helper
76	// lookup to a binary no podman setup has.
77	const credentialHelperPrefix = "docker-credential-"
78	
79	func (cliRunner) Run(dc dockerCmd) ([]byte, error) {
80		shape := engine.Current()
81		name := shape.Binary
82		if dc.Helper != "" {
83			name = credentialHelperPrefix + dc.Helper
84		}
85		cmd := exec.Command(name, dc.Args...) //nolint:gosec // helper name comes from the engine's own auth file
86		if dc.Ctx != nil {
87			cmd = exec.CommandContext(dc.Ctx, name, dc.Args...) //nolint:gosec // same argument as above
88		}
89		if dc.Stdin != "" {
90			cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(dc.Stdin)
91		}
92		if dc.Combined {
93			return cmd.CombinedOutput()
94		}
95		return cmd.Output()
96	}
97	
98	// runner is swapped by tests via stubRunner. Production code never reassigns
99	// it — switching engines changes what cliRunner reads, not which runner is
100	// installed — so the package stays safe to call concurrently; tests that swap
101	// it must not run in parallel.
102	var runner dockerRunner = cliRunner{}
103	
104	// requireEngine reports the absence of the container engine, naming the one
105	// that was actually looked for rather than "docker" — someone who pinned podman
106	// is not helped by being told docker is missing.
107	func requireEngine() error {
108		if err := runner.LookPath(); err != nil {
109			return fmt.Errorf("%s not found: %w", engine.Current().Name, err)
110		}
111		return nil
112	}
113	
114	// cmdLabel builds the prefix a failed invocation is reported under — "docker
115	// stop", "podman network create". It is what the footer shows (Rule 128), so it
116	// names the engine in use rather than the one this package was first written
117	// against.
118	//
119	// Not called `label`: every reporting helper below already takes a `label`
120	// parameter, and a function of that name would be shadowed inside each of them.
121	func cmdLabel(subcommand string) string {
122		return engine.Current().Name + " " + subcommand
123	}
124	
125	// templates is the set of --format strings for the engine in use.
126	func templates() engine.Templates { return engine.Current().Templates }
127	
128	// dockerOutput runs `<engine> args...` and returns stdout only.
129	func dockerOutput(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
130		return runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args})
131	}
132	
133	// dockerCombined runs `<engine> args...` and returns stdout and stderr merged.
134	func dockerCombined(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
135		return runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true})
136	}
137	
138	// wrapErr reports a failed invocation whose stderr was not captured, keeping the
139	// underlying error for errors.Is/As.
140	func wrapErr(label string, err error) error {
141		return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %w", label, err)
142	}
143	
144	// errWithOutput reports a failed invocation using the captured output, which
145	// carries the engine's own diagnostic.
146	func errWithOutput(label string, output []byte) error {
147		return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
148	}
149	
150	// mutate runs a subcommand whose output only matters on failure, and wraps that
151	// output in an error prefixed with label (e.g. "docker stop failed"). Callers
152	// build the label with cmdLabel, so it names the engine actually in use.
153	//
154	// It leaves Ctx at its zero value: nothing stops these, which is D7's answer
155	// for every mutating call but the pull.
156	func mutate(label string, args ...string) error {
157		output, err := runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true})
158		return mutationError(label, output, err)
159	}
160	
161	// mutateContext is mutate for the one call that can be stopped.
162	func mutateContext(ctx context.Context, label string, args ...string) error {
163		output, err := runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true, Ctx: ctx})
164		return mutationError(label, output, err)
165	}
166	
167	// mutationError turns a captured invocation into the error both mutators
168	// report, using the engine's own diagnostic.
169	func mutationError(label string, output []byte, err error) error {
170		if err != nil {
171			return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
172		}
173		return nil
174	}
175	
176	// prune runs a prune subcommand and returns its trimmed report.
177	func prune(label string, args ...string) (string, error) {
178		output, err := dockerCombined(args...)
179		if err != nil {
180			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
181		}
182		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
183	}
184	
185	// splitLines splits trimmed command output into non-empty lines.
186	func splitLines(output []byte) []string {
187		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
188		if trimmed == "" {
189			return nil
190		}
191		var lines []string
192		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(trimmed, "\n") {
193			if line != "" {
194				lines = append(lines, line)
195			}
196		}
197		return lines
198	}

28		// cannot be aggregated: it is a share of *this* container's limit, so two
29		// of them are fractions of different wholes (see Aggregate).

37		BlockTX    int64  // block bytes written (parsed from BlockIO)

40	// ListContainers returns a list of containers. If all is true, includes stopped containers.
41	func ListContainers(all bool) ([]Container, error) {
42		if err := requireEngine(); err != nil {
43			return nil, err
44		}
45	
46		args := []string{"ps"}
47		if all {
48			args = append(args, "--all")

50		args = append(args, "--format", templates().PS)
51	
52		output, err := dockerOutput(args...)

54			return nil, wrapErr(cmdLabel("ps"), err)
55		}
56	
57		var containers []Container
58		for _, line := range splitLines(output) {
59			parts := strings.SplitN(line, "\t", 7)
60			if len(parts) < 4 {
61				continue
62			}
63			c := Container{
64				ID:    parts[0],
65				Name:  parts[1],
66				Image: parts[2],
67				State: parts[3],
68			}
69			if len(parts) > 4 {
70				c.Status = parts[4]
71				c.Facts = ParseStatus(c.Status)
72			}
73			if len(parts) > 5 {

75			}
76			if len(parts) > 6 {

78			}

80		}
81	
82		return containers, nil
83	}

87		if err := requireEngine(); err != nil {

89		}

59	type cliRunner struct{}
60	
61	func (cliRunner) LookPath() error {
62		_, err := exec.LookPath(engine.Current().Binary)
63		return err
64	}
65	
66	func (cliRunner) Build(args ...string) *exec.Cmd {
67		return exec.Command(engine.Current().Binary, args...) //nolint:gosec // the binary is a declared engine name or a path the user configured
68	}
69	
70	// credentialHelperPrefix names a credential helper binary, under both engines.
71	//
72	// Podman does not have a prefix of its own: measured on 2026-09-25, podman
73	// 5.7.0 with `credHelpers: {"host": "fake"}` ran docker-credential-fake for
74	// both `get` and `store` while a podman-credential-fake sat next to it on
75	// PATH, never called. A podman-specific prefix (§3.67) sent every helper
76	// lookup to a binary no podman setup has.
77	const credentialHelperPrefix = "docker-credential-"
78	
79	func (cliRunner) Run(dc dockerCmd) ([]byte, error) {
80		shape := engine.Current()
81		name := shape.Binary
82		if dc.Helper != "" {
83			name = credentialHelperPrefix + dc.Helper
84		}
85		cmd := exec.Command(name, dc.Args...) //nolint:gosec // helper name comes from the engine's own auth file
86		if dc.Ctx != nil {
87			cmd = exec.CommandContext(dc.Ctx, name, dc.Args...) //nolint:gosec // same argument as above
88		}
89		if dc.Stdin != "" {
90			cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(dc.Stdin)
91		}
92		if dc.Combined {
93			return cmd.CombinedOutput()
94		}
95		return cmd.Output()
96	}
97	
98	// runner is swapped by tests via stubRunner. Production code never reassigns
99	// it — switching engines changes what cliRunner reads, not which runner is
100	// installed — so the package stays safe to call concurrently; tests that swap
101	// it must not run in parallel.
102	var runner dockerRunner = cliRunner{}
103	
104	// requireEngine reports the absence of the container engine, naming the one
105	// that was actually looked for rather than "docker" — someone who pinned podman
106	// is not helped by being told docker is missing.
107	func requireEngine() error {
108		if err := runner.LookPath(); err != nil {
109			return fmt.Errorf("%s not found: %w", engine.Current().Name, err)
110		}
111		return nil
112	}
113	
114	// cmdLabel builds the prefix a failed invocation is reported under — "docker
115	// stop", "podman network create". It is what the footer shows (Rule 128), so it
116	// names the engine in use rather than the one this package was first written
117	// against.
118	//
119	// Not called `label`: every reporting helper below already takes a `label`
120	// parameter, and a function of that name would be shadowed inside each of them.
121	func cmdLabel(subcommand string) string {
122		return engine.Current().Name + " " + subcommand
123	}
124	
125	// templates is the set of --format strings for the engine in use.
126	func templates() engine.Templates { return engine.Current().Templates }
127	
128	// dockerOutput runs `<engine> args...` and returns stdout only.
129	func dockerOutput(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
130		return runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args})
131	}
132	
133	// dockerCombined runs `<engine> args...` and returns stdout and stderr merged.
134	func dockerCombined(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
135		return runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true})
136	}
137	
138	// wrapErr reports a failed invocation whose stderr was not captured, keeping the
139	// underlying error for errors.Is/As.
140	func wrapErr(label string, err error) error {
141		return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %w", label, err)
142	}
143	
144	// errWithOutput reports a failed invocation using the captured output, which
145	// carries the engine's own diagnostic.
146	func errWithOutput(label string, output []byte) error {
147		return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
148	}
149	
150	// mutate runs a subcommand whose output only matters on failure, and wraps that
151	// output in an error prefixed with label (e.g. "docker stop failed"). Callers
152	// build the label with cmdLabel, so it names the engine actually in use.
153	//
154	// It leaves Ctx at its zero value: nothing stops these, which is D7's answer
155	// for every mutating call but the pull.
156	func mutate(label string, args ...string) error {
157		output, err := runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true})
158		return mutationError(label, output, err)
159	}
160	
161	// mutateContext is mutate for the one call that can be stopped.
162	func mutateContext(ctx context.Context, label string, args ...string) error {
163		output, err := runner.Run(dockerCmd{Args: args, Combined: true, Ctx: ctx})
164		return mutationError(label, output, err)
165	}
166	
167	// mutationError turns a captured invocation into the error both mutators
168	// report, using the engine's own diagnostic.
169	func mutationError(label string, output []byte, err error) error {
170		if err != nil {
171			return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
172		}
173		return nil
174	}
175	
176	// prune runs a prune subcommand and returns its trimmed report.
177	func prune(label string, args ...string) (string, error) {
178		output, err := dockerCombined(args...)
179		if err != nil {
180			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %s", label, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
181		}
182		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
183	}
184	
185	// splitLines splits trimmed command output into non-empty lines.
186	func splitLines(output []byte) []string {
187		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
188		if trimmed == "" {
189			return nil
190		}
191		var lines []string
192		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(trimmed, "\n") {
193			if line != "" {
194				lines = append(lines, line)
195			}
196		}
197		return lines
198	}

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"

8	)

10	// Container represents a Docker container with its metrics
11	type Container struct {
12		ID        string
13		Name      string
14		Image     string
15		State     string // running, exited, paused, created, restarting, dead
16		Status    string // "Up 2 hours", "Exited (0) 5min ago"
17		CreatedAt string // "2 hours ago"
18		// Facts is what Status says, parsed once here so views never read
19		// Docker's wording. See ParseStatus.
20		Facts StatusFacts
21		// Ports is parsed here rather than carried as the string docker printed:
22		// the view must not learn to read Docker's output, and an opaque string
23		// cannot be searched by port number. See ParseContainerPorts.
24		Ports      []PortBinding
25		CPUPercent float64
26		MemUsage   string // "150MiB / 8GiB"
27		// MemBytes is the used half of MemUsage. It exists because MemPercent
28		// cannot be aggregated: it is a share of *this* container's limit, so two
29		// of them are fractions of different wholes (see Aggregate).
30		MemBytes   int64
31		MemPercent float64
32		NetIO      string // "1.2kB / 3.4kB"
33		NetRX      int64  // received bytes (parsed from NetIO)
34		NetTX      int64  // transmitted bytes (parsed from NetIO)
35		BlockIO    string // "1.2MB / 3.4MB"
36		BlockRX    int64  // block bytes read (parsed from BlockIO)
37		BlockTX    int64  // block bytes written (parsed from BlockIO)
38	}
39	
40	// ListContainers returns a list of containers. If all is true, includes stopped containers.
41	func ListContainers(all bool) ([]Container, error) {
42		if err := requireEngine(); err != nil {
43			return nil, err
44		}
45	
46		args := []string{"ps"}
47		if all {
48			args = append(args, "--all")
49		}
50		args = append(args, "--format", templates().PS)
51	
52		output, err := dockerOutput(args...)
53		if err != nil {
54			return nil, wrapErr(cmdLabel("ps"), err)
55		}
56	
57		var containers []Container
58		for _, line := range splitLines(output) {
59			parts := strings.SplitN(line, "\t", 7)
60			if len(parts) < 4 {
61				continue
62			}
63			c := Container{
64				ID:    parts[0],
65				Name:  parts[1],
66				Image: parts[2],
67				State: parts[3],
68			}
69			if len(parts) > 4 {
70				c.Status = parts[4]
71				c.Facts = ParseStatus(c.Status)
72			}
73			if len(parts) > 5 {
74				c.CreatedAt = parts[5]
75			}
76			if len(parts) > 6 {
77				c.Ports = ParseContainerPorts(parts[6])
78			}
79			containers = append(containers, c)
80		}
81	
82		return containers, nil
83	}

1	// Package engine names the container engine DevDesk drives — docker or podman —
2	// and carries everything about it that is not the same between the two.
3	//
4	// It exists as its own package rather than as a field of internal/docker
5	// because internal/scan needs the same answer and does not import
6	// internal/docker. That is the internal/forge arrangement read one level down:
7	// the thing every caller shares does not live inside one of its callers.
8	//
9	// What a Shape carries is what measurement, not taste, put there (§3.67):
10	//
11	//   - the binary, which is the cheap part — internal/docker already funnels
12	//     every invocation through one runner;
13	//   - the credential helper prefix and the auth file, because that file is read
14	//     *and written* directly rather than through the CLI;
15	//   - the host socket, which is the one path that breaks rather than moves:
16	//     rootless podman has no /var/run/docker.sock, and its own socket exists
17	//     only while `podman system service` runs;
18	//   - the output templates, which are the silent risk. See Templates.
19	//
20	// Nothing here sniffs. A shape is declared, the way a forge's is and the way a
21	// registry's `provider` is (§3.8): a thing is treated as what it says it is.
22	package engine
23	
24	import (
25		"fmt"
26		"os/exec"
27		"path/filepath"
28		"strings"
29		"sync"
30	)
31	
32	// Shape is one container engine: what to run, where it keeps its credentials,
33	// and how to ask it for machine-readable output.
34	type Shape struct {
35		// Name identifies the engine for a config discriminator, a log line, and
36		// the word the views show — "docker", "podman".
37		Name string
38	
39		// Binary is what gets executed. It is the engine's own name for the two
40		// declared shapes, and an explicit path when the configuration names one.
41		Binary string
42	
43		// Templates are the --format strings for every output this application
44		// parses.
45		Templates Templates
46	}
47	
48	// A Shape carries no resolved filesystem path, and that is deliberate: the
49	// credential file and the socket are looked up through AuthPaths(), AuthPath()
50	// and HostSocket() at the moment they are needed.
51	//
52	// Storing them on the struct was tried and reverted. The shape is built once,
53	// at package initialisation, so a $HOME or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR read there is
54	// frozen before anything else runs — and the socket is worse, since whether it
55	// exists is the entire question and it can appear (`podman system service`) or
56	// vanish while the application is up. A cached answer to "where is the file"
57	// is a cached answer to "does it exist", which is not a thing a shape can know
58	// once and for all.
59	
60	// Templates holds one Go template per parsed output.
61	//
62	// They are a field of the shape rather than constants at the call sites for a
63	// reason a real podman went on to confirm: podman implements --format, but
64	// equality of the *fields* is guaranteed nowhere. A divergence does not
65	// always raise an error and produce a wrong row (the defect class this
66	// repository keeps cataloguing, D24, D25, D57) — three of the twelve outputs
67	// (Info, NetworkLS, SystemDF) name a field podman's template engine does not
68	// have at all, which fails the command outright instead. `podman info`
69	// exiting 125 on every poll is what host capacity looked like before this was
70	// measured.
71	//
72	// The other nine match dockerTemplates exactly against that same podman, so
73	// they stay unified rather than being forked speculatively. What this
74	// indirection buys is that a future divergence is one line here rather than a
75	// refactor. Do not collapse it back into constants (§3.67).
76	//
77	// The twelfth parsed output has no template and is not here: `system df -v` is
78	// a fixed-width table scraped by column offsets (internal/docker/images.go),
79	// because no --format exposes per-image unique size. See ParsesSystemDFVerbose.
80	type Templates struct {
81		// PS lists containers: id, name, image, state, status, created, ports.
82		PS string
83		// PSState asks for nothing but the state column, to count containers.
84		PSState string
85		// Stats is the live resource sample, taken with --no-stream.
86		Stats string
87		// Info is the host's capacity: CPU count and total memory.
88		Info string
89		// ImageLS lists images: id, repository, tag, size, created.
90		ImageLS string
91		// ImageInspect reads the size and the registry digests of several images
92		// in one call.
93		ImageInspect string
94		// ImageRepoDigests reads one image's registry digests as JSON.
95		ImageRepoDigests string
96		// ImageExposedPorts reads an image's EXPOSE declarations as JSON.
97		ImageExposedPorts string
98		// NetworkLS lists networks: id, name, driver, scope, created.
99		NetworkLS string
100		// VolumeLS lists volumes: name, driver, mountpoint.
101		VolumeLS string
102		// SystemDF is the disk report, one row per resource family.
103		SystemDF string
104		// Version is the client version, for the dashboard's tools table.
105		Version string
106	}
107	
108	// ParsesSystemDFVerbose reports whether `<engine> system df -v` prints the
109	// fixed-width "Images space usage:" table internal/docker scrapes for per-image
110	// unique size and container count.
111	//
112	// Only docker is known to. Under podman the columns are left empty rather than
113	// filled from offsets taken on a header that may not be the same one: a blank
114	// column reads as an absence, a value sliced out of the wrong column does not.
115	func (s Shape) ParsesSystemDFVerbose() bool { return s.Name == Docker }
116	
117	// Engine names, shared with the configuration. They are duplicated in
118	// internal/config rather than imported from it so that config does not depend
119	// on this package; TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape holds the two in step,
120	// the same arrangement the forge names have (§3.6).
121	const (
122		// Docker is what `auto` resolves to when both engines are installed, and
123		// what an unrecognised name falls back to.
124		Docker = "docker"
125		Podman = "podman"
126	)
127	
128	// Auto asks for whichever engine is installed. It is the default, so that
129	// nobody who installed exactly one of the two is asked which one they meant —
130	// app.secret_backend's precedent (§3.9).
131	const Auto = "auto"
132	
133	// dockerTemplates is the set every call in this application was written
134	// against. podmanTemplates is a copy, and stays a copy until the measurement
135	// described on Templates has been made.
136	var dockerTemplates = Templates{
137		PS:                "{{.ID}}\t{{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.CreatedAt}}\t{{.Ports}}",
138		PSState:           "{{.State}}",
139		Stats:             "{{.ID}}\t{{.CPUPerc}}\t{{.MemUsage}}\t{{.MemPerc}}\t{{.NetIO}}\t{{.BlockIO}}",
140		Info:              "{{.NCPU}}\t{{.MemTotal}}",
141		ImageLS:           "{{.ID}}\t{{.Repository}}\t{{.Tag}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{.CreatedAt}}",
142		ImageInspect:      "{{.ID}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{json .RepoDigests}}",
143		ImageRepoDigests:  "{{json .RepoDigests}}",
144		ImageExposedPorts: "{{json .Config.ExposedPorts}}",
145		NetworkLS:         "{{.ID}}\t{{.Name}}\t{{.Driver}}\t{{.Scope}}\t{{.CreatedAt}}",
146		VolumeLS:          "{{.Name}}\t{{.Driver}}\t{{.Mountpoint}}",
147		SystemDF:          "{{.Type}}\t{{.TotalCount}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{.Reclaimable}}",
148		Version:           "{{.Client.Version}}",
149	}
150	
151	// podmanTemplates diverges from dockerTemplates on the three outputs measured
152	// against a real `podman system service` (§3.67): Info, NetworkLS and
153	// SystemDF each name a docker-only struct field, and podman's template
154	// engine — unlike its JSON output, which does carry the docker-shaped field
155	// under a different name or nested — fails the whole command rather than
156	// leaving the field blank. `podman info` exits 125 outright, which is what
157	// broke host capacity reporting for every podman user; the other two return
158	// no rows.
159	//
160	//   - Info: podman nests CPU count and memory under .Host, not at the root.
161	//     This is also the field `dk setup`'s container-engine question caught,
162	//     via `docker.FetchCapacity` erroring outright on a genuinely running
163	//     podman instead of reporting it unreachable for some other reason.
164	//   - NetworkLS: podman networks carry no scope (docker's Scope column is a
165	//     swarm concept), and podman's field is called Created, not CreatedAt.
166	//     The Scope segment is left empty rather than guessed at "local" — the
167	//     same call HostSocket makes about reporting an absence as a fact.
168	//   - SystemDF: podman's template-formatted row exposes Total, not the
169	//     TotalCount its own `--format json` uses for the same count.
170	//
171	// The other nine outputs were checked against the same podman and matched
172	// dockerTemplates exactly, so they are not copied here.
173	var podmanTemplates = func() Templates {
174		t := dockerTemplates
175		t.Info = "{{.Host.CPUs}}\t{{.Host.MemTotal}}"
176		t.NetworkLS = "{{.ID}}\t{{.Name}}\t{{.Driver}}\t\t{{.Created}}"
177		t.SystemDF = "{{.Type}}\t{{.Total}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{.Reclaimable}}"
178		return t
179	}()
180	
181	// current is the resolved engine. It starts as docker so that every caller has
182	// a usable answer before the router has read a configuration — which is what
183	// the application did before this package existed, and what a test that never
184	// resolves anything should keep seeing.
185	var (
186		currentMu sync.RWMutex
187		current   = shapeFor(Docker, Docker)
188	)
189	
190	// Current returns the engine in use.
191	func Current() Shape {
192		currentMu.RLock()
193		defer currentMu.RUnlock()
194		return current
195	}
196	
197	// SetCurrent installs the resolved engine. The router calls it once at startup
198	// and once per context switch, from Update — never from a Cmd (Rule 110).
199	func SetCurrent(s Shape) {
200		currentMu.Lock()
201		defer currentMu.Unlock()
202		current = s
203	}
204	
205	// Names lists the engines a shape is declared for, in the order the
206	// configuration view cycles them.
207	func Names() []string { return []string{Docker, Podman} }
208	
209	// Resolve turns an app.container_engine value into the engine to drive.
210	//
211	// The four cases:
212	//
213	//	""/"auto"  docker if it is on PATH, else podman, else an error naming both
214	//	"docker"   pinned; absent is an error
215	//	"podman"   pinned; absent is an error
216	//	anything   taken as a path to a binary
217	//
218	// A pinned engine that is not installed is an error rather than a fall back to
219	// the other one. That is credentials.Select's rule (§3.9), and for the same
220	// reason: someone who asked for podman should not silently get docker, because
221	// the two do not hold the same containers.
222	func Resolve(preference string) (Shape, error) {
223		switch preference {
224		case "", Auto:
225			for _, name := range Names() {
226				if _, err := exec.LookPath(name); err == nil {
227					return shapeFor(name, name), nil
228				}
229			}
230			return Shape{}, fmt.Errorf("no container engine found: neither %s nor %s is on PATH", Docker, Podman)
231	
232		case Docker, Podman:
233			if _, err := exec.LookPath(preference); err != nil {
234				return Shape{}, fmt.Errorf("%s not found: %w", preference, err)
235			}
236			return shapeFor(preference, preference), nil
237		}
238	
239		// Anything else is a path. The engine it belongs to is read from the file
240		// name — the one place this package guesses, and it guesses about a value
241		// the user typed rather than about the world. Getting it wrong costs the
242		// auth file location, not the invocation.
243		path := preference
244		if _, err := exec.LookPath(path); err != nil {
245			return Shape{}, fmt.Errorf("container engine %q not found: %w", path, err)
246		}
247		return shapeFor(engineOfPath(path), path), nil
248	}
249	
250	// engineOfPath reads an engine name out of a configured path. Everything that
251	// is not recognisably podman is treated as docker, which is what an unknown
252	// docker-compatible CLI (nerdctl, a wrapper script) behaves like.
253	func engineOfPath(path string) string {
254		base := strings.ToLower(filepath.Base(path))
255		base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, ".exe")
256		if strings.HasPrefix(base, Podman) {
257			return Podman
258		}
259		return Docker
260	}
261	
262	// shapeFor builds the shape for one engine, running the given binary.
263	func shapeFor(name, binary string) Shape {
264		if name == Podman {
265			return Shape{
266				Name:      Podman,
267				Binary:    binary,
268				Templates: podmanTemplates,
269			}
270		}
271		return Shape{
272			Name:      Docker,
273			Binary:    binary,
274			Templates: dockerTemplates,
275		}
276	}
277	
278	// ShapeFor returns the declared shape for an engine name, running that name as
279	// its binary. It answers the configuration view, which needs the shapes before
280	// anything has been resolved — internal/forge's reason for holding its shapes
281	// in a table rather than on its backends.
282	func ShapeFor(name string) Shape { return shapeFor(name, name) }
283

780	1. `scan.image_verification: off` pulls the tag, as before §3.82.
781	2. `~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is read on every pull. A file that does not load
782	   **refuses** the pull, naming the error: an unreadable policy is not an empty
783	   one, and falling back to the built-in rules would drop the user's in silence.
784	3. The tag is resolved to a digest (`oci.ManifestDigest`, the index digest
785	   cosign signs). A registry that will not give it is a Failed verdict decided
786	   by the rule that would have applied — a user rule refuses, anything else
787	   pulls the tag and warns.
788	4. `trust.Evaluate` on that digest, with the local image of the same repository
789	   (`RepoDigests`) for continuity. `Block` is an `imagepull.BlockedError`,
790	   whose message is the reason, naming the rule.
791	5. `pull repo@digest`, then `docker.TagImage` back to the name asked for.
792	   Pulling the tag instead would let it move between the check and the pull —
793	   the attack. Measured on Docker and Podman; under Docker's containerd store
794	   `repo@sha256:…` also shows in `RepoTags`, `docker images` lists one row.
795	
796	What the views do with it: a refusal is a footer **Error** naming the rule, and
797	the `:jobs` detail an agent reads is the same sentence; a Warn goes ahead and
798	says why after the pull. The Images tab header shows `Signatures: off`, or
799	`trust.yaml invalid` — read once when the view starts (`checkTrustPolicyCmd`).
800	
801	**The `Sig` column** of the Images tab (`signatures.go`, the shared
802	`internal/ui/sigcol`) is each local image's verdict on the content on disk:
803	`imagepull.LocalDigest` picks the `RepoDigests` entry of the image's own
804	repository, and `imagepull.Check` asks about that digest against the rules
805	alone — continuity would compare the image with itself. An image with no such
806	digest was built or loaded here (a hammer, as in Update). Checked in the
807	background on `ImagesListMsg`, four at a time; `sigAsked` keeps the digest each
808	image was asked about, so an unchanged list asks nothing, a pull that changes
809	the digest asks again, a verdict about a former digest is dropped, and a Failed
810	one is retried after 30 minutes. An image no rule covers is decided without
811	cosign, and one DevDesk pulled comes from the verdict cache. Nothing acts on
812	the column.
813	
814	**`run` never pulls**: `buildLaunchArgs` and `VerifyEntrypoint` pass
815	`--pull=never` (a missing image exits 125, both engines). An image reaches the
816	machine through a verified pull or not at all. DevDesk's own tool images —
817	Trivy, cosign, the netdiag image — are pulled by their `run` and are **not**
818	verified: a declared exception.
819	
820	## Network Diagnostics View
821	
822	`internal/ui/netdiag/` — five tabs:
823	- **Diagnostics tab** (`model.go`): target, port and resolver, then
824	  `internal/netcheck`'s pipeline — resolve, route, reach, connect, TLS, HTTP —
825	  chained one stage per message so the footer can name the question being asked.
826	  The seven tool checkboxes are gone (§3.33): the checks follow from the target
827	  and from what has already failed.
828	- **Ports tab** (`ports_model.go`): the machine's own socket table, re-read
829	  every `ports_refresh_interval`, filtered by protocol, state and text. `K`
830	  terminates a process, after a confirmation. It runs **no container** — see
831	  `internal/ports` below. Column 0 is the activity column (DEVDESK-150, below).
832	- **Interfaces tab** (`interfaces_model.go`): this machine's network interfaces
833	  — name, state, MTU, MAC, RX/TX error counters, addresses — in a `datatable`.
834	  It runs **no container**; see `internal/netiface` below. It was the Topology
835	  tab, and §3.44 is why three of its four sections are gone rather than
836	  translated.
837	- **Forward tab** (`forward_model.go`, `forward_form.go`): the port
838	  redirections, `N` to open one, `space` to pause or resume it and `K` to delete
839	  it. It holds **no listener** — see `internal/forward` below.
840	- **Path tab** (`path_model.go`, `path_view.go`, `path_run.go`,
841	  `path_target.go`, `path_from_route.go`, `path_steps.go`; DEVDESK-328,
842	  DEVDESK-329): the hop-by-hop path to
843	  a target, from `internal/nettrace` (below). It is the fifth and last tab
844	  (`tabPath = 4`, `tabCount = 5`). It runs **no container**. Three states:
845	  `pathEditing` (the target field has the keyboard), `pathRunning` (field
846	  blurred, hops arriving) and `pathDone` (hops kept on screen). The **body is
847	  always the hop table** (`PathModel.view()` returns `table.View()`, Rule 139),
848	  in every state: columns Hop, Step, Address, RTT, with a silent hop dim and
849	  never red. **The column starts on this machine** (DEVDESK-329): three local
850	  rows, then the hops. `source` reads `this machine`; `interface` reads
851	  `<name> (<source address>)`; `gateway` reads the gateway address. The local
852	  rows have an empty Hop and RTT (they asked nobody; `-` means "no answer") and
853	  the default text colour. `pathSteps` (`path_steps.go`) is the only place that
854	  orders the rows; the table item is a `pathStep` (kind source, interface,
855	  gateway or hop). Nothing is shown before the route is known, so a resolution
856	  error leaves 0 rows. The **target field is not in the body**: it sits in the footer's
857	  bar slot, framed by `components.BarFrame` (`Target › ` + the field,
858	  placeholder `hostname or IPv4 address[:port]`). That slot is shown on this
859	  tab in every state, so `GetFooterHeight()` is 5 (bar 2, tab row 1, blank
860	  line 1, info line 1) and the layout does not move between editing, running
861	  and done. The tab keeps its own `FooterMessage`, returned by `activeFooter`,
862	  so `WantsBlink()` follows a running trace. `Model.Running()` is true while a
863	  trace runs, so the router does not rebuild the view mid-trace.
864	
865	  Keys: `enter` launches (while editing) or traces again (when done); `esc`
866	  cancels a running trace, and returns a finished one to editing with the
867	  value kept; `tab` switches tab; `up`, `down`, `pgup`, `pgdown`, `home` and
868	  `end` move in the table in every state. While editing, `esc`, `tab` and
869	  `shift+tab` do nothing in the field. A paste reaches the field only while
870	  editing (Rule 111). A changed field value clears the persistent error.
871	
872	**Ports tab, terminal blurred (DEVDESK-210).** `PortsModel.unfocused` is set by
873	`shared.TerminalFocusMsg`, which `netdiag.Model.Update` forwards to the ports
874	poll whichever tab shows (the tick runs on every tab). The tick chain is kept:
875	`handleTick` re-arms `portsTickCmd` and skips `fetchPortsCmd` while `unfocused`.
876	On the focus edge (`Resume`) it reads once, with no new tick, so the chain is
877	not doubled. `unfocused` is separate from `paused`, the user's own pause (shown
878	in the bar): a user pause is never lifted by a focus, and the resume read is
879	skipped while `paused`.
880	
881	**Ports tab, activity column (DEVDESK-150, Rule 125).** Column 0 of the socket
882	table is `datatable.IndicatorColumn` (untitled, two cells wide), the same
883	mechanism as `oci/images` (DEVDESK-146). The table has no registry run: `K` is
884	held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID, and `datatable` writes the
885	precedence "busy means `indicator.Running`" once, so the column's own state is
886	always `Idle` and an idle row shows an empty cell (a socket has no rest icon).
887	
888	- **`K` running = lit dot.** Every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○`, as the
889	  spinner did before. The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`, handled in
890	  `Model.Update` (`SetBlinkPhase`, nothing rebuilt); `Model.WantsBlink()` is true
891	  while any row is busy, whatever the active tab. The Diagnostics and Interfaces
892	  footers show the same shared dot while a run or an interfaces read is in
893	  flight (DEVDESK-373), driven by the same `FrameMsg`: `WantsBlink()` is also
894	  true while the active tab's footer is on `Activity`. The `netdiag` package
895	  holds no `spinner.Model` and no `spinner.TickMsg` handler.
896	- **The line spinner is gone**: `StatusColumn`, `portsSpinnerTickMsg`,
897	  `portsSpinnerCmd` and `handleSpinnerTick` are deleted. **State keeps its
898	  text** (`LISTEN`), dimmed like every busy row. This reverses the letter of
899	  §3.22 (the State cell used to be replaced by the spinner) and keeps its intent:
900	  the dim says the value is about to change.
901	- **The footer names the kill**: for the selected busy row, `● Killing sshd (812)`
902	  (`PortsModel.rowDetail`, from `components.DescribeRow`), before the
903	  paused or stale text. At 60 columns, where PID and Process are dropped, this is
904	  where the process name is readable.
905	- **Failure stays in the footer only.** A refused or failed kill is an `Error`
906	  (`killFailureMessage`) and the row returns to rest: no `⊗`, nothing is
907	  remembered, because no registry kind exists for it. `K` stays lit on a busy
908	  row (Rule 130); pressing it again warns `Already killing PID N`.
909	- **A periodic refresh never blinks**: `SetItems` leaves `busy` alone, so a
910	  refresh with nothing busy leaves column 0 empty and `WantsBlink()` false; one
911	  during a kill keeps the dots and the cursor.
912	- **A failed network test is not a row operation.** The Diagnostics table keeps
913	  its result in the Verdict column; no `⊗` was added (open question 4 of the
914	  activity-indicator stories, option A). The Diagnostics and Interfaces tables
915	  have no `Indicator`; neither does the Path tab's hop table (DEVDESK-328): a
916	  trace is one run, not a per-row operation, and its running state is the
917	  footer's shared dot. The Path files `path_model.go`, `path_target.go` and
918	  `path_view.go` (and, since DEVDESK-329, `path_steps.go`) are in the activity guard's scanned sources for
919	  `command.ViewNetdiag`; `path_run.go`, which holds the I/O, is not.
920	- **Files.** `ports_activity.go` (`ActivityTables()` reports `netdiag/ports`,
921	  `WantsBlink()`); `ports_commands.go` holds the I/O commands (`fetchPortsCmd`,
922	  `portsTickCmd`, `killProcessCmd`) and `NewPortsDataMsg`, which the activity
923	  guard's footer seed uses to hand rows to the view without reading the socket
924	  table. `ports_commands.go` is not scanned by the guard (its refresh tick is
925	  data, not a row animation).
926	- **Widths (Rule 116).** Required columns give way rightmost first. Thresholds,
927	  as terminal width, with the column added (they were 99, 87, 78 and 50 before):
928	
929	  | Columns shown | From width |
930	  |---|---|
931	  | all | 103 |
932	  | without Process | 91 |
933	  | without PID and Process | 82 |
934	  | activity, Proto, State, Local Address | 54 |
935	
936	  At 60 columns the last set shows and `RenderedWidth()` is 58.
937	
938	**Timing (§3.66).** `netcheck.Check` carries a `Duration time.Duration`
939	alongside `Summary`/`Facts` — zero means untimed. `stage_connect.go` and
940	`stage_tls.go` fill it from the dial and the handshake respectively;
941	`stage_http.go` fills it from an `httptrace.ClientTrace` attached in
942	`env.go`'s `Head`, which also gives `HTTPResult` a DNS/connect/TLS/TTFB
943	breakdown surfaced as `Facts` on the `HTTP` row. Nothing keeps a history
944	across runs — that stays an open question.
945	
946	That breakdown also drives a waterfall: `Check.Phases` is a set of named,
947	non-overlapping spans that sum exactly to `Duration` (nil on checks with
948	nothing to break down — TCP, TLS). `stage_http.go`'s `httpPhases` derives
949	**Wait** and **Content** rather than charting TTFB directly, because TTFB is
950	measured from the start of the request and already contains DNS+connect+TLS —
951	charting it as a fifth independent share would double-count that overlap.
952	`internal/ui/netdiag/view.go`'s `phaseLines` renders one proportional bar per
953	phase, reusing the load-gauge machinery (`theme.GaugeFill`, `GaugeTrack`,
954	`GaugeFillWidth`, `GaugeTrackStyle`) with a new neutral fill colour, `theme.TimingFillStyle` —
955	a phase taking most of the time is a fact to read, not a severity to spot.
956	
957	**Opened prefilled, from elsewhere (§3.66).** `netdiag.NewWithTarget` builds a
958	view with the form filled in but not yet run; `netdiag.OpenRequestMsg` is
959	what a producer elsewhere sends to ask the router for one (mirroring
960	`uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg`), and `netdiag.BackToOriginMsg` is how `esc` gets
961	back out, via `Model.OriginView` — empty when netdiag was opened directly
962	from the command line, in which case `esc` behaves exactly as it always has.
963	`status`'s `H` (`keymap.Diagnose`, `internal/ui/status/diagnostics.go`) is
964	the first producer: it resolves the selected monitor's target and
965	auto-runs the pipeline when the port is certain (http/https/ssl), or lands on
966	the prefilled form when it is a guess (icmp/dns).
967	
968	`H` has a **second producer, inside netdiag** (DEVDESK-328,
969	`path_from_route.go`): on the Diagnostics results, with the **Local route** row
970	(`netcheck.CheckRoute`) selected, it switches to the Path tab and fills the
971	target field with the results' host. It **prefills and never launches**:
972	nothing is resolved or sent until `enter` on the Path tab. Only the host is
973	carried over, not the port (the route check does not depend on one).
974	`pathFromRoute()` is the one availability read by the header (the entry
975	`H Trace the path` is greyed off the route row, Rule 130) and by the handler,
976	which otherwise warns `Select the Local route row to trace its path`. If a
977	trace is already running, `H` switches to the Path tab, leaves the field
978	alone and warns `A path trace is already running — esc cancels it` on the Path
979	footer. `PathModel.prefill` puts the tab back in editing with the hops, the
980	outcome and the error cleared.
981	
982	**What is configurable, and what is not.** `internal/netcheck` held its timeouts
983	as constants with a comment saying they would become settings when somebody
984	asked; `network:` is what they became.
985	
986	| Setting | Replaces |
987	|---|---|
988	| `check_timeout` | five per-stage constants — 5 s for DNS and the dial, 8 s for TLS and HTTP, 4 s for the ping |
989	| `ping_count` | `pingCount` |
990	| `cert_expiry_warn_days` | `expiryWarnWindow` |
991	| `ports_refresh_interval` | the 2 s tick |
992	
993	**One timeout replaces five**, and the default is the old *maximum* so nothing
994	that answers today starts failing. The 5 / 5 / 8 / 8 / 4 split was never argued
995	anywhere — five rows for one idea, and each of the five a separate guess. The
996	cost is stated rather than discovered: an unreachable host now spends 8 s on DNS
997	instead of 5, which the staged progress line makes legible rather than a hang.
998	
999	`traceroute_max_hops` was a sixth setting and went with the trace it bounded
1000	(§3.47). It stays removed: the trace is back in the process (DEVDESK-327, see
1001	[The path trace](#the-path-trace--internalnettrace)), but `nettrace.Options.MaxHops`
1002	is not wired to any setting, and the Path tab (DEVDESK-328) still traces with
1003	the engine's defaults (`nettrace.Options{}`).
1004	
1005	Two things stay hardcoded, each for a reason:
1006	
1007	- **`MinVersion: VersionTLS10`** — the handshake is *probing*, not securing.
1008	  Reporting an old version is the point; a setting could only make the tool
1009	  blind to what it exists to find.
1010	- **`InsecureSkipVerify`** — the TLS stage verifies the chain itself so it can
1011	  say *which* part failed. A setting here would collapse four checks into one
1012	  error string.
1013	
1014	`netcheck.Settings` travels **beside** `Env`, not on it: `Env` is the seam to
1015	the network, while `PingCount` and `ExpiryWarnWindow` are read by stages and
1016	never by a network call — putting a preference behind the seam would make every
1017	fake answer for one. `Settings.Normalized()` fills in anything non-positive at
1018	every entry point, so a hand-edited `0` becomes the default rather than a dial
1019	with no deadline. The view calls `checkSettings()` per run rather than capturing
1020	at construction, so a run already in flight and the config cannot disagree
1021	halfway down the pipeline.
1022	
1023	Every probe here answers from the DevDesk process. The route trace was the one
1024	exception and §3.47 removed it: `--network host` on Docker Desktop is the VM's
1025	namespace, so it traced a path from somewhere else. It is back, in the process,
1026	since DEVDESK-327 (`internal/nettrace`, below). Nothing shells out.
1027	
1028	**The `route` stage answers the question no other check can** (§3.44): when a
1029	VPN captures the default route, a host that is plainly reachable elsewhere is
1030	unreachable here, and every other row reports the *symptom* — no ICMP reply, no
1031	TCP connect — while none reports the cause. `Env.Route(ctx, ip)` returns a
1032	`RouteHop{Interface, Source, Gateway}`, and the summary names the **interface**
1033	because that is what the user recognises: "Traffic leaves through ProtonVPN"
1034	answers the question, `10.2.0.1` needs a second lookup to mean anything.
1035	
1036	`github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` is what makes it one implementation instead of
1037	three — `GetBestRoute2` on Windows, an `RTM_GETROUTE` netlink query on Linux, the
1038	routing socket on the BSDs — with no privilege anywhere and ~2 ms per lookup,
1039	measured. It depends only on `x/net` and `x/sys`, both already in the graph.

  the default text colour. `pathSteps` (`path_steps.go`) is the only place that
  orders the rows; the table item is a `pathStep` (kind source, interface,
  gateway or hop). Nothing is shown before the route is known, so a resolution
  error leaves 0 rows. The **target field is not in the body**: it sits in the footer's
  bar slot, framed by `components.BarFrame` (`Target › ` + the field,
  placeholder `hostname or IPv4 address[:port]`). That slot is shown on this
  tab in every state, so `GetFooterHeight()` is 5 (bar 2, tab row 1, blank
  line 1, info line 1) and the layout does not move between editing, running
  and done. The tab keeps its own `FooterMessage`, returned by `activeFooter`,
  so `WantsBlink()` follows a running trace. `Model.Running()` is true while a
  trace runs, so the router does not rebuild the view mid-trace.

  Keys: `enter` launches (while editing) or traces again (when done); `esc`
  cancels a running trace, and returns a finished one to editing with the
  value kept; `tab` switches tab; `up`, `down`, `pgup`, `pgdown`, `home` and

  `shift+tab` do nothing in the field. A paste reaches the field only while
  editing (Rule 111). A changed field value clears the persistent error.

`shared.TerminalFocusMsg`, which `netdiag.Model.Update` forwards to the ports
poll whichever tab shows (the tick runs on every tab). The tick chain is kept:
`handleTick` re-arms `portsTickCmd` and skips `fetchPortsCmd` while `unfocused`.
On the focus edge (`Resume`) it reads once, with no new tick, so the chain is
not doubled. `unfocused` is separate from `paused`, the user's own pause (shown
in the bar): a user pause is never lifted by a focus, and the resume read is
skipped while `paused`.

**Ports tab, activity column (DEVDESK-150, Rule 125).** Column 0 of the socket
table is `datatable.IndicatorColumn` (untitled, two cells wide), the same
mechanism as `oci/images` (DEVDESK-146). The table has no registry run: `K` is
held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID, and `datatable` writes the
precedence "busy means `indicator.Running`" once, so the column's own state is
always `Idle` and an idle row shows an empty cell (a socket has no rest icon).

- **`K` running = lit dot.** Every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○`, as the
  spinner did before. The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`, handled in
  `Model.Update` (`SetBlinkPhase`, nothing rebuilt); `Model.WantsBlink()` is true
  while any row is busy, whatever the active tab. The Diagnostics and Interfaces
  footers show the same shared dot while a run or an interfaces read is in
  flight (DEVDESK-373), driven by the same `FrameMsg`: `WantsBlink()` is also
  true while the active tab's footer is on `Activity`. The `netdiag` package
  holds no `spinner.Model` and no `spinner.TickMsg` handler.
- **The line spinner is gone**: `StatusColumn`, `portsSpinnerTickMsg`,
  `portsSpinnerCmd` and `handleSpinnerTick` are deleted. **State keeps its
  text** (`LISTEN`), dimmed like every busy row. This reverses the letter of
  §3.22 (the State cell used to be replaced by the spinner) and keeps its intent:
  the dim says the value is about to change.
- **The footer names the kill**: for the selected busy row, `● Killing sshd (812)`
  (`PortsModel.rowDetail`, from `components.DescribeRow`), before the
  paused or stale text. At 60 columns, where PID and Process are dropped, this is
  where the process name is readable.
- **Failure stays in the footer only.** A refused or failed kill is an `Error`
  (`killFailureMessage`) and the row returns to rest: no `⊗`, nothing is
  remembered, because no registry kind exists for it. `K` stays lit on a busy
  row (Rule 130); pressing it again warns `Already killing PID N`.
- **A periodic refresh never blinks**: `SetItems` leaves `busy` alone, so a
  refresh with nothing busy leaves column 0 empty and `WantsBlink()` false; one
  during a kill keeps the dots and the cursor.
- **A failed network test is not a row operation.** The Diagnostics table keeps
  its result in the Verdict column; no `⊗` was added (open question 4 of the
  activity-indicator stories, option A). The Diagnostics and Interfaces tables
  have no `Indicator`; neither does the Path tab's hop table (DEVDESK-328): a
  trace is one run, not a per-row operation, and its running state is the
  footer's shared dot. The Path files `path_model.go`, `path_target.go` and
  `path_view.go` (and, since DEVDESK-329, `path_steps.go`) are in the activity guard's scanned sources for
  `command.ViewNetdiag`; `path_run.go`, which holds the I/O, is not.
- **Files.** `ports_activity.go` (`ActivityTables()` reports `netdiag/ports`,
  `WantsBlink()`); `ports_commands.go` holds the I/O commands (`fetchPortsCmd`,
  `portsTickCmd`, `killProcessCmd`) and `NewPortsDataMsg`, which the activity
  guard's footer seed uses to hand rows to the view without reading the socket
  table. `ports_commands.go` is not scanned by the guard (its refresh tick is
  data, not a row animation).

  as terminal width, with the column added (they were 99, 87, 78 and 50 before):

  | Columns shown | From width |
  |---|---|
  | all | 103 |
  | without Process | 91 |
  | without PID and Process | 82 |
  | activity, Proto, State, Local Address | 54 |

alongside `Summary`/`Facts` — zero means untimed. `stage_connect.go` and
`stage_tls.go` fill it from the dial and the handshake respectively;
`stage_http.go` fills it from an `httptrace.ClientTrace` attached in
`env.go`'s `Head`, which also gives `HTTPResult` a DNS/connect/TLS/TTFB
breakdown surfaced as `Facts` on the `HTTP` row. Nothing keeps a history
across runs — that stays an open question.

That breakdown also drives a waterfall: `Check.Phases` is a set of named,
non-overlapping spans that sum exactly to `Duration` (nil on checks with
nothing to break down — TCP, TLS). `stage_http.go`'s `httpPhases` derives
**Wait** and **Content** rather than charting TTFB directly, because TTFB is
measured from the start of the request and already contains DNS+connect+TLS —
charting it as a fifth independent share would double-count that overlap.

phase, reusing the load-gauge machinery (`theme.GaugeFill`, `GaugeTrack`,
`GaugeFillWidth`, `GaugeTrackStyle`) with a new neutral fill colour, `theme.TimingFillStyle` —
a phase taking most of the time is a fact to read, not a severity to spot.

**Opened prefilled, from elsewhere (§3.66).** `netdiag.NewWithTarget` builds a
view with the form filled in but not yet run; `netdiag.OpenRequestMsg` is
what a producer elsewhere sends to ask the router for one (mirroring
`uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg`), and `netdiag.BackToOriginMsg` is how `esc` gets
back out, via `Model.OriginView` — empty when netdiag was opened directly
from the command line, in which case `esc` behaves exactly as it always has.

the first producer: it resolves the selected monitor's target and
auto-runs the pipeline when the port is certain (http/https/ssl), or lands on
the prefilled form when it is a guess (icmp/dns).

`H` has a **second producer, inside netdiag** (DEVDESK-328,
`path_from_route.go`): on the Diagnostics results, with the **Local route** row
(`netcheck.CheckRoute`) selected, it switches to the Path tab and fills the
target field with the results' host. It **prefills and never launches**:
nothing is resolved or sent until `enter` on the Path tab. Only the host is
carried over, not the port (the route check does not depend on one).
`pathFromRoute()` is the one availability read by the header (the entry
`H Trace the path` is greyed off the route row, Rule 130) and by the handler,
which otherwise warns `Select the Local route row to trace its path`. If a
trace is already running, `H` switches to the Path tab, leaves the field
alone and warns `A path trace is already running — esc cancels it` on the Path
footer. `PathModel.prefill` puts the tab back in editing with the hops, the
outcome and the error cleared.

**What is configurable, and what is not.** `internal/netcheck` held its timeouts
as constants with a comment saying they would become settings when somebody
asked; `network:` is what they became.

| Setting | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `check_timeout` | five per-stage constants — 5 s for DNS and the dial, 8 s for TLS and HTTP, 4 s for the ping |
| `ping_count` | `pingCount` |
| `cert_expiry_warn_days` | `expiryWarnWindow` |
| `ports_refresh_interval` | the 2 s tick |

**One timeout replaces five**, and the default is the old *maximum* so nothing
that answers today starts failing. The 5 / 5 / 8 / 8 / 4 split was never argued
anywhere — five rows for one idea, and each of the five a separate guess. The
cost is stated rather than discovered: an unreachable host now spends 8 s on DNS
instead of 5, which the staged progress line makes legible rather than a hang.

`traceroute_max_hops` was a sixth setting and went with the trace it bounded
(§3.47). It stays removed: the trace is back in the process (DEVDESK-327, see
[The path trace](#the-path-trace--internalnettrace)), but `nettrace.Options.MaxHops`
is not wired to any setting, and the Path tab (DEVDESK-328) still traces with
the engine's defaults (`nettrace.Options{}`).

Two things stay hardcoded, each for a reason:

- **`MinVersion: VersionTLS10`** — the handshake is *probing*, not securing.
  Reporting an old version is the point; a setting could only make the tool
  blind to what it exists to find.
- **`InsecureSkipVerify`** — the TLS stage verifies the chain itself so it can
  say *which* part failed. A setting here would collapse four checks into one
  error string.

`netcheck.Settings` travels **beside** `Env`, not on it: `Env` is the seam to
the network, while `PingCount` and `ExpiryWarnWindow` are read by stages and
never by a network call — putting a preference behind the seam would make every
fake answer for one. `Settings.Normalized()` fills in anything non-positive at
every entry point, so a hand-edited `0` becomes the default rather than a dial
with no deadline. The view calls `checkSettings()` per run rather than capturing
at construction, so a run already in flight and the config cannot disagree
halfway down the pipeline.

Every probe here answers from the DevDesk process. The route trace was the one
exception and §3.47 removed it: `--network host` on Docker Desktop is the VM's
namespace, so it traced a path from somewhere else. It is back, in the process,
since DEVDESK-327 (`internal/nettrace`, below). Nothing shells out.

**The `route` stage answers the question no other check can** (§3.44): when a
VPN captures the default route, a host that is plainly reachable elsewhere is
unreachable here, and every other row reports the *symptom* — no ICMP reply, no
TCP connect — while none reports the cause. `Env.Route(ctx, ip)` returns a
`RouteHop{Interface, Source, Gateway}`, and the summary names the **interface**
because that is what the user recognises: "Traffic leaves through ProtonVPN"
answers the question, `10.2.0.1` needs a second lookup to mean anything.

`github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` is what makes it one implementation instead of
three — `GetBestRoute2` on Windows, an `RTM_GETROUTE` netlink query on Linux, the
routing socket on the BSDs — with no privilege anywhere and ~2 ms per lookup,
measured. It depends only on `x/net` and `x/sys`, both already in the graph.

1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
7		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
10	)
11	
12	// ChoiceModal asks "which of these actions, or none".
13	//
14	// ConfirmModal poses a closed question and OptionConfirmModal a closed
15	// question paired with a variant; neither one can offer two distinct
16	// actions. §3.26 needs this for `K`: stop and restart are two gestures, not
17	// one gesture and its modifier — a restart is a stop followed by a start,
18	// and presenting the second as a checkbox of the first would turn an
19	// exclusive choice into a toggle (Rule 132).
20	//
21	// Cancel is the default choice, like "No" elsewhere (Rule 104): both of
22	// these actions cut ongoing connections.
23	type ChoiceModal struct {
24		title   string
25		message string
26		choices []string
27		// focused indexes choices, and equals len(choices) on Cancel — which is
28		// therefore always the last button, without needing to be in the list.
29		focused int
30		width   int
31		height  int
32	}
33	
34	// NewChoiceModal creates a modal with N actions plus Cancel, focused on Cancel.
35	func NewChoiceModal(title, message string, choices ...string) *ChoiceModal {
36		return &ChoiceModal{
37			title:   title,
38			message: message,
39			choices: choices,
40			focused: len(choices), // Cancel
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// ChoiceModalPickedMsg is sent when the user picks an action.
45	// Index and Label refer to the same thing: the index for routing, the label
46	// for logging without having to re-translate it.
47	type ChoiceModalPickedMsg struct {
48		Index int
49		Label string
50	}
51	
52	// ChoiceModalCancelledMsg is sent when the user gives up.
53	type ChoiceModalCancelledMsg struct{}
54	
55	// Update updates the modal.
56	func (m *ChoiceModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ChoiceModal, tea.Cmd) {
57		switch msg := msg.(type) {
58		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
59			m.width = msg.Width
60			m.height = msg.Height
61	
62		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
63			switch msg.String() {
64			// ←/→ between buttons (Rule 135 — Tab is reserved for tabs). The
65			// traversal is bounded rather than cyclic: Cancel must stay the end
66			// of the run, otherwise one extra press would loop back onto an action.
67			case "left":
68				m.focused = max(m.focused-1, 0)
69				return m, nil
70	
71			case "right":
72				m.focused = min(m.focused+1, len(m.choices))
73				return m, nil
74	
75			case "enter":
76				return m, m.pick()
77	
78			case "esc":
79				return m, cancelChoice
80			}
81		}
82	
83		return m, nil
84	}
85	
86	// pick returns the command matching the focused button.
87	func (m *ChoiceModal) pick() tea.Cmd {
88		if m.focused >= len(m.choices) {
89			return cancelChoice
90		}
91		picked := ChoiceModalPickedMsg{Index: m.focused, Label: m.choices[m.focused]}
92		return func() tea.Msg { return picked }
93	}
94	
95	func cancelChoice() tea.Msg { return ChoiceModalCancelledMsg{} }
96	
97	// View renders the modal.
98	func (m *ChoiceModal) View() string {
99		var b strings.Builder
100	
101		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
102		b.WriteString("\n\n")
103		b.WriteString(m.message)
104		b.WriteString("\n\n")
105	
106		// The actions are "danger" and Cancel is "primary", the same split as
107		// Yes/No: it's the safe button that carries the calm color.
108		buttons := make([]string, 0, len(m.choices)+1)
109		for i, choice := range m.choices {
110			buttons = append(buttons, theme.RenderButton(choice, m.focused == i, "danger"))
111		}
112		buttons = append(buttons, theme.RenderButton("Cancel", m.focused == len(m.choices), "primary"))
113	
114		b.WriteString(strings.Join(buttons, theme.Bg("  ")))
115		b.WriteString("\n\n")
116	
117		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
118			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
119			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
120			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder()).
121			BorderForeground(theme.ColorError).
122			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground).
123			Padding(1, 2).
124			Render(b.String())
125	}
126
